cfn_corpus_scope.note: AWS intros target the CFN-registry corpus (sdk/providers/descriptions/aws.json, 1,437 resource types), scoped explicitly to exclude the 1,684-page HashiCorp corpus, which is being moved to aws-hashicorp/ and kept as-is rather than improved this phase. The 7 pre-existing hand-authored entries (aws_s3_bucket, aws_ecr_repository, aws_sqs_queue, aws_iam_policy, aws_iam_role, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment, aws_vpc) predate this scoping and are HashiCorp-named; they are left in place, not part of CFN batch counting below.

intros.sourcing_notes: Batch 1 of the AWS CFN corpus (indices 0-96 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_access_analyzer_analyzer through aws_app_test_test_case). 57 of 97 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept (IAM Access Analyzer, AWS Private CA, Bedrock AgentCore Agent Registry, CloudWatch AIOps investigation groups, Amazon MQ brokers, AWS Amplify Hosting, Amplify UIBuilder, Amazon API Gateway REST APIs resources/stages/usage plans, AppConfig's full application/environment/deployment/experimentation surface, Amazon AppFlow, AppIntegrations, App Mesh's core mesh/node/router/service components, App Runner, WorkSpaces Applications (the renamed Amazon AppStream 2.0), AppSync GraphQL APIs and Events, and AWS Mainframe Modernization Application Testing). 40 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service (a usage-plan key against its usage plan, a v2 API Gateway sub-resource against the v2 API concept, an AppStream fleet/stack/entitlement association against the resource it associates, an AppSync API key or domain name against the GraphQL API it authorizes or fronts), the same parent-concept pattern proven across the prior five providers, most densely in this batch across API Gateway v1/v2's many sub-resources. 0 genuine skips: every one of the 97 real overview or reference pages fetched returned substantive content. Two notable non-recency findings surfaced live rather than assumed: AWS App Mesh carries an end-of-support notice (discontinued September 30, 2026, in favor of Amazon ECS Service Connect) and AWS App Runner is no longer open to new customers, both real, current vendor-page facts folded into their own intros rather than written as if the services were in normal active growth. Amazon AppStream 2.0 was verified live to have been renamed Amazon WorkSpaces Applications, with a real, newly expanded concepts page (agent sessions, computer use, an MCP service for AI agents) alongside its original fleet/stack/image-builder/app-block model; directory_config and entitlement, absent from that renamed concepts page, were confirmed real and still documented via a second, more targeted search rather than being assumed stale or skipped, the same two-search minimum the ticket's own GCP rollout_plan precedent established. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 97 (aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_target). Batch 2 (indices 97-196 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_target through aws_certificate_manager_certificate). 80 of 100 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept, spanning Application Auto Scaling, Application Insights, Application Signals, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, ARC Region switch and zonal autoshift, Athena, Audit Manager, EC2 Auto Scaling and Auto Scaling Plans, AWS B2B Data Interchange, AWS Backup (including its Audit Manager sub-feature, legal holds, air-gapped vaults, and restore testing), AWS Batch (including 2025's consumable-resource scheduling and SageMaker service environments), AWS Billing and Cost Management's newer BCM Dashboard/Pricing Calculator/Data Exports surface, Billing Conductor, custom billing views, Amazon Braket, AWS Budgets, the entire Amazon Bedrock core surface (agents, knowledge bases, guardrails, automated reasoning checks, flows, prompt management, inference profiles, intelligent prompt routing, sessions, data automation), the entire Amazon Bedrock AgentCore surface (runtime, memory, gateway with rate limiting, identity/OAuth2, browser and code interpreter tools, harness, evaluations, payments, capacity providers), Connect Cases, Amazon Keyspaces, Cost Explorer's anomaly detection and cost categories, and AWS Certificate Manager. 20 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service, most densely across Bedrock AgentCore's gateway sub-resources (target, rate limit, rule) and its dataset/evaluator pairing, and across AWS Backup's restore-testing plan/selection and framework/report-plan pairing. 0 genuine skips: every one of the 100 real overview or reference pages fetched returned substantive content. Bedrock's own core service page surfaced a real, current status finding rather than an assumption: Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Bedrock Agents Classic) is no longer open to new customers, superseded by Bedrock AgentCore, mirroring Batch 1's App Runner and App Mesh findings; AWS Audit Manager was independently confirmed to be in the same no-new-customers state. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore itself, along with roughly a third of this batch (Application Signals, AMP anomaly detection, ARC Region switch, Batch consumable resources and service environments, most of the BCM surface, Bedrock's automated reasoning checks, session management, and the entire AgentCore payments/harness/evaluations surface), are genuinely 2024-2026 features verified live via WebSearch, several from mid-to-late 2025 and 2026, well past the point memory alone would be reliable, the same discipline Kubernetes and GCP Compute established earlier in this phase. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 197.

last_migration.stopped_at: Migration complete for what exists: all 30,142 real entries from ubiquex/sdk/providers/descriptions/aws.json (CFN vendor + DeepSeek AI) plus the 7 hand-authored docs pages are in descriptions.json. Real gap, not a stopping point to resume from: 1,085 of the SDK artifact's 1,437 CFN-derived resource types (89.4% by count) use a naming convention (underscore-split CFN service names, e.g. aws_access_analyzer_analyzer) that does not match the live docs corpus's own HashiCorp-derived naming (aws_accessanalyzer_analyzer) -- only 352 resource types share a name. Next real onboarding session: decide whether AWS's docs corpus adopts CFN naming on its next regeneration (making the other 1,085 entries immediately usable) or whether a real alias/rename table is needed.
